items.note: Both: soft brush/water, AR coating, 10 deg tilt, weekly-ish in dry season. Neither asks for hot-spot/cracked-glass inspection or names flour dust.
Both inspect for white rust/pitting and retorque quarterly + post-monsoon. X also fits isolating pads (root-cause fix); Y adds frame-bond continuity test instead.
Both check latch, heat marks, chafe, ties quarterly. Y explicitly says the insulation test does not show hot MC4s; X frames the gap as wake-up-only/after-breach. Both meet rule 4.

Both: breathing/no drain/top vent/flour dust, gentle vent cleaning, yearly vent. Both weekly in monsoon, monthly otherwise (key: monthly / 3-monthly). Neither suggests desiccant or relocating vent/adding drain.

items.item: LiFePO4 heat ageing (sensor gap: BMS temp)
items.y_refs: C27, C01, C14, C39, Sec.3 item 3
items.note: Both measure cabinet/outer-cell temps vs cell 8 monthly and shade parking. Y adds yearly capacity test (exactly half key's 6-month frequency, boundary-accurate); X has no capacity tracking.
Both: Al creep, no spring washers, vibration, torque to cell maker, IR under load. X retorque monthly (key quarterly); Y 50 h then quarterly + rough tows.
Both: partial SOC, open isolator, check/recharge every 4 weeks; both note the 12 mA BMS draw continues. X 60-70% SOC vs key 50-60% (close).
Both retighten studs and cage terminals, fit ferrules, early first check, then quarterly (2x key frequency, within band).

items.item: Motor cable flex fatigue at swinging plate
items.note: Both identify gland-exit fatigue and Hall cores failing first. X monthly (key 3-monthly); Y 250 h + each tow. Neither adds strain relief.
Both clean cowl/fins weekly, daily in heavy dust. X also checks fan for cracks.
Both: light oil not grease, free-swing check. Y oils every 250 h (~half key frequency, boundary) with a weekly free-swing check and play check.

items.y_refs: C07, C12, C17, C37, C33, Sec.3 item 2
items.note: Both compare rpm to 440 each use and recognise the 250 rpm gap; replace at END. X rib inspection weekly (~25-40 h, key 100 h); Y rib inspection every 250 h (pointer weekly). Y adds alignment check.
Both check set screw, key, taper-lock. Y has early 20-50 h re-check and post-tow; X monthly, no run-in check. Neither mentions thread-locker.
Both: measured 2-3 g H1 every 250 h, never pump to resistance, check play, reset locknut. X play check monthly (more often than key 500 h); Y adds yearly reseal/repack.

items.item: Upper bearing outer-ring creep in Al housing
items.note: Both state the Al/steel expansion creep mechanism and inspect the bore. Y dial-indicator check every 500 h matches key; X periodic check is monthly hand/IR feel, bore checked at stones-off service. Neither suggests retaining compound/sleeve.

items.item: Spindle bearing false brinelling in towing
items.note: Both name false brinelling and do a post-tow hand-turn check; X adds moderate speed. Neither unloads/supports the runner stone before towing (the key preventive action), so Partly for both.
Both measure furrows and thickness vs 30 mm groove and dress/replace as pair. X monthly (~100-130 h) with dressing 300-600 h; Y every 250 h (key inspect 100 h).
Both compute ~2,600 flexes/min, note finger falls below the magnet. Both inspect daily/each use (key 100 h).
Both clean each use.
Both dry-clean daily, inspect sweepers, clean before storage.
Y explicitly warns against lubricating them (abrasive paste, food path). X only notes they run dry; no warning, so not Caught per rule 3. Y bush inspection 250 h vs key 100 h.
Both explicit, citing the Sorel bond.
X tests E-stop, hopper 60 s stop, and NTC/rpm plausibility. Y tests E-stop and checks readings but only cleans the hopper sensor; no functional test of the 60 s stop, so Partly.

verdict: No meaningful difference. Both checklists score 44/46 with 21 Caught, 2 Partly and 0 Missed, and both catch all 3 sensor-gap items. Neither contains harmful advice. Y is ahead on the traps (2/2 vs 1/2: only Y warns against lubricating the dry-running UHMW-PE feed bushes). Y's intervals are also closer to the key (16 Accurate vs 14). Y adds a pre-tow motor-plate restraint, a frame-bond continuity test and a yearly reseal of the lower bearing. X never sets an interval too rare (0 vs 3: Y's belt rib, stone and spout-bush inspections at 250 h are too rare). X also functionally tests the hopper sensor and fits isolating pads at the PV clamps. Its errors are all on the side of checking too often (7 items), plus a wrong hours-to-calendar conversion for greasing. An owner would be well served by either; these trade-offs roughly cancel out.
